A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same investigation of visual information extraction from a shared CLIP encoder, with overlapping authors, experiments, and results. Their main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite extensive revision and retitling.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark evaluations, CLIP/SigLIP/XVLM finetuning experiments, and LLaVA decoding and relaxed-matching experiments in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains original evaluations and reports additional experiments involving token usage, position embeddings, stronger text encoders, contrastive conversion, and question prompts.

M1.justification: V2 introduces substantial experimental model adaptations: [CLS]-only LLaVA, PACL patch aggregation with RoPE, SPARC-style token interaction, and question-conditioned LLaVA-VLM2Vec trained contrastively. The stronger-text-encoder experiment changes from Llama-2/LLM2Vec to Llama-3/LLM2CLIP. These alter architectures, inputs, aggregation procedures, and training objectives.

E1.justification: V2 adds actual evaluations on Winoground, NaturalBench-R, SugarCREPE, and SeeTrue, substantially expanding compositional reasoning and image-text alignment coverage. Appendix B.6 additionally evaluates EqBen-mini and COCOCounterfactuals. The spatial and MMVP benchmarks and LLaVA training datasets remain represented.

E2.justification: V2 adds Phi-3-V-3.8B and LLaMA-3-V-8B to comparisons on retained benchmarks, plus an evaluated LLM2CLIP checkpoint in Table 6. XVLM-COCO disappears, although XVLM-16M remains. The M3ID comparison removes RP and DIVA; I-MoF remains, moving from a numerical prose comparison into Table 14.

E3.justification: V2 adopts fixed-template VQAScore for the main MLLM evaluations, replacing v1's primary response-based approach and letter-perplexity control. It changes the stated MMVP matching direction to caption-wise matching and adds SeeTrue AUROC. New training designs include 10 epochs with batch size 4096 for patch-token experiments and 900 steps with batch size 256 for VLM2Vec. Standard CLIP/SigLIP finetuning retains five epochs and batch size 512; the relaxed-pair evaluation is removed.

E4.justification: V2 adds ablations of [CLS] versus patch tokens, RoPE, multiple text tokens, contrastive conversion, and question removal in Tables 5-7. Appendices A.3 and B.6 add evaluation-method comparisons and cases where CLIP performs better. V1's relaxed-matching probe and LLM2Vec combinations are removed. The M3ID analysis is retained in Appendix B.7, not newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed lists, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. V2 continues reporting point estimates; its new aggregate benchmark bars do not introduce uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive benchmark and ablation results, including VLM2Vec pair accuracy of 95.1% with a question versus 0.0% without one on What’sUp A Left/Right. Its LLaVA MMVP VQAScore pair accuracy is 36.0%, under a different protocol from v1's 25.3% response-based result. Original What’sUp response results and M3ID scores survive in Tables 10 and 14. V1's relaxed-matching scores of 64.0% and 73.3%, and its LLM2Vec result rows, are removed.

T1.justification: V1's explicit erroneous-agreement threshold, cosine-versus-Spearman vector counterexample, and relaxed-matching inequality are removed. V2 supplies patch-aggregation equations in Section 3.2. These are limited changes to definitions and short mathematical arguments; neither version develops a theorem or proof framework.

C1.justification: The retained central observation is that a fixed CLIP encoder preserves information that downstream processing can exploit. V2 redefines the contribution around specific architectural factors—patch tokens, positions, and question-conditioned embeddings—and claims that generation and autoregressive finetuning are unnecessary for strong reasoning. This substantially revises v1's emphasis on erroneous agreements and its proposed cosine/contrastive-paradigm bottleneck.

C2.justification: V2 explains the gap through local and positional information and question-dependent patch weighting, replacing v1's more abstract alignment explanation. It drops the relaxed-evaluation 'upper bound' interpretation. New limitations restrict conclusions to the studied encoder/model pairs, and Appendix B.6 discusses CLIP-favorable cases and possible benchmark-construction effects. The computing-resource limitation is retained.

D1.justification: V2 substantially expands reproducibility information through checkpoint links and license statements, training times, LoRA settings, augmentation and caption-processing instructions, and detailed PACL/SPARC embedder specifications in Appendices A.2 and B.1-B.5. It also discloses four-way response prompts. The existing standard finetuning recipe is largely retained; the additional budgets principally describe new experiments.

R1.justification: V1's broad positioning around VLM blindness, hallucination, and decoding is substantially refocused on alignment, token usage, and promptable embeddings. V2 adds substantive engagement with PACL, SPARC, LLM2CLIP, VLM2Vec, CLOC, VQAScore, and newer compositionality studies, while removing much of the earlier hallucination and decoding literature.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled and extensively rewrites its abstract, introduction, investigation, discussion, and conclusion around a broader architectural explanation. Related work is integrated into the discussion, M3ID moves to the appendix, limitations become a separate section, and the appendices are substantially reorganized and expanded.

P2.justification: The single-column preprint becomes a two-column document. Figure 1 is redrawn with a new accuracy-summary plot, and the experimental roadmap is substantially expanded. V1's evaluation illustration moves to Appendix A.1 as Figure 3, while its MMVP example figure disappears. Tables are extensively rebuilt, expanded, reduced, and redistributed.

improvement.justification: V1 largely inferred a paradigm bottleneck and explicitly deferred detailed dissection. V2 distinguishes and tests [CLS] versus patch outputs and adds position, prompt-removal, and contrastive-conversion experiments in Sections 3.2-3.4, substantially strengthening the central explanation. Additional model families and CLIP-favorable cases improve its evidential scope and qualifications. Some earlier diagnostics are removed, and performance-driven prompt selection and absent uncertainty estimates remain limitations, but the explanatory and empirical gains are substantial.
